qs.q:
Learning Foreign Languages — Which person…

A=Alan (communicative learner; ignores structure; speaks regardless of mistakes; thanked shop assistant for correcting pronunciation)
B=Ben (friend advised memorising 50 words; compiled script of useful phrases; language-immersion meet-up group; needs to focus on grammar in future)
C=Celine (reads comics while commuting; moved to adapted readers; writes translation in margins; highlights useful structures)
D=David (B2 in Italian but can't speak to native speakers; instructors only taught vocab from bilingual lists; recalling in real-life is tough)
E=Eve (keen traveller; volunteered worldwide; picked up basics in several languages; singing improved pronunciation; mastered idioms)
F=Fiona (native speakers consider her gifted; records herself speaking; listens back; replaces familiar words with synonyms; checks progress)

0. is an auditory learner? [E=Eve]
1. believes that determination, formal education and practice lead to success?
2. has difficulty when speaking the language?
3. uses a wide range of activities to get exposed to the new language?
4. is particularly interested in expanding vocabulary?
5. is entirely self-taught?
6. doesn't worry about making mistakes?
7. is aware of multiple connotations of words?
8. likes to get feedback from native speakers?
9. has gradually improved their reading skill?
10. blames the teaching methods for lack of language competence?
11. plans to upgrade their grammar?
12. learns through images?
items: 1 — believes that determination, formal education and practice lead to success?
2 — has difficulty when speaking the language?
3 — uses a wide range of activities to get exposed to the new language?
4 — is particularly interested in expanding vocabulary?
7 — is aware of multiple connotations of words?
8 — likes to get feedback from native speakers?
9 — has gradually improved their reading skill?
10 — blames the teaching methods for lack of language competence?

qs.q:
Woman Completes Quest to Eat One Scone in Every UK Legacy Property

"Where PRIDE OF PLACE is taken by a pile of warm, fluffy scones smothered in clotted cream."

The author considers…
A scones to be excessively British.
B scones the focal point of afternoon tea.
C British people to be very proud of scones.
D cream and strawberry jam the ultimate topping.
opts: scones the focal point of afternoon tea.
British people to be very proud of scones.
cream and strawberry jam the ultimate topping.

qs.q:
Woman Completes Quest…

"...described by fellow Brits in terms ranging from 'ODD' to 'FUNNY IN THE HEAD'."

According to the author, British people…
A found Betty's quest eccentric.
B considered Betty's behaviour amusing.
C thought Betty spent too much time on her quest.
D did not believe that Betty would complete the project.
opts: thought Betty spent too much time on her quest.
did not believe that Betty would complete the project.

qs.q:
Woman Completes Quest…

"'I'M NEVER, EVER SICK OF SCONES!' said the 45-year-old travel agent."

Betty Masters…
A remains a fan of scones.
B has never been ill after eating a scone.
C distributed scones to a group of reporters.
D did not believe she would complete her quest.
opts: has never been ill after eating a scone.
distributed scones to a group of reporters.
did not believe she would complete her quest.

qs.q:
Woman Completes Quest…

"For their annual subscription of £50 per year, its 7.5 million members have a FREE PASS to the organisation's many sites."

UK Legacy members do NOT…
A mind which causes they support.
B have to show their badges on entry.
C receive public recognition for their work.
D have to pay to enter individual properties.
opts: have to show their badges on entry.
receive public recognition for their work.
have to pay to enter individual properties.

The Power of Influencers

"Whereas some influencers can attribute their popularity to sophisticated education and exceptional expertise, others monetise their charisma or a sense of humour. They often focus on niches – specific segments within a broader market or field. (19) ____. By creating compelling content related to corresponding products or services, they inspire millions of people worldwide."

A Their audiences are smaller but even more closely-knit communities of buyers with similar needs.
B That is how they foster wider audience engagement and consequently create revenue.
C They would have done anything to attract new subscribers or followers.
D The implications of this newfound power can indeed be disheartening.
E Selling products and services had always required a lot of knowledge and skill.
F The connection between influencers and followers is immediate, creating a sense of intimacy.
G Some influencers have been criticised for promoting products they do not use or genuinely believe in.
H These can range from fashion and beauty to fitness, travel, or technology.
opts: A — Their audiences are smaller but more closely-knit communities.
B — That is how they foster wider audience engagement.
C — They would have done anything to attract new subscribers.
D — The implications of this newfound power can be disheartening.
E — Selling products had always required knowledge and skill.
F — The connection between influencers and followers is immediate.
G — Some influencers have been criticised for promoting products they don't use.
H — These can range from fashion and beauty to fitness, travel, or technology.
